title: dForge Module Triggers
description: Trigger definitions for a dForge module (logic/triggers.json). A trigger watches an entity for an event (insert/update/delete/status_change/any), evaluates an optional formula condition using `[field]` syntax, and fires an action if true. Different from scheduled jobs (cron-driven) and webhooks (outbound HTTP) — triggers are intra-tenant DB-event-driven action invocations.

code.description: Trigger code, unique within the module.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the trigger does and when.

entity.description: Entity whose events this trigger watches. May be cross-module via dot notation (e.g. 'fin.invoice').

event.description: DB event that fires this trigger. 'status_change' only fires when the entity's status field actually changes value. 'any' fires for all insert/update/delete.

condition.description: Optional formula expression — same shape as canExecute in action DSL. Uses `[field]` syntax to reference the affected record. Single-line, evaluates to boolean. If omitted, trigger fires for every matching event. Reference navigation (`[ref].[target]`) is REJECTED here: the event-time evaluator only reads columns of the changed row, so a nav path would resolve to null and the trigger would misfire. Navigate inside the action instead, or denormalise the value onto the watched entity.

action.description: Action code to invoke. The trigger binds the affected record to the action as RECORD CONTEXT, so the action reads its columns with `[field]` (and its PK with `[pk_column]`) exactly like a UI-invoked action — no lookup needed. The action's `entityCode` MUST equal this trigger's `entity`, and its `executionMode` must not be `batch`; both are enforced at pack time. Cross-module references use the qualified form 'module.action'.

params.description: Optional STATIC parameters passed to the action at invocation time — the literal values written here, nothing else. Nothing is injected at runtime: there is no `record_id` param. The affected record arrives as record context (`[field]`), and its pre-change values as `old[field]` on update/delete/status_change events.

async.description: When true (the default), the action runs in the background — the triggering transaction commits before the action starts. Recommended for slow actions (emails, external API calls); background failures are logged, not surfaced to the caller. When false, the action runs synchronously inside the same transaction as the triggering insert/update/delete: if the action fails (e.g. calls error()), the whole mutation rolls back and the error is returned to the caller — so an async:false trigger can undo the user's write. Keep async:false actions fast; they run on the request's transaction.
